text:
dana: Quick follow-up thread from today's all-hands re: security/privacy/compliance. I'll log decisions, links, and owners here. Ping me if I mis-summarize.
priya: SOC2 Q: are we going for Type I or Type II? and what scope (hosted vs private)?
dana: Planning SOC2 Type II covering Hosted API + Dedicated (control plane + serving). Private deployments will be in scope for contractual attestations but customers are generally responsible for their on-prem controls; we will offer audit evidence packages for Private installs where we maintain control plane components.
sam: ISO27001 status? Roadmap alignment with SOC2 audit?
dana: ISO27001 is scheduled as a follow-on. We want SOC2 Type II first to solidify operational evidence. ISO planning is in product for H1 next year; cross-team gap analysis starts next quarter.
leo: VPC / network isolation question: if a customer uses Redwood Private in their VPC, do we ever need to open outbound ports for telemetry/ops?
ana: Private deploys can be fully air-gapped if customer chooses. Default Private deployment uses an operator that performs periodic check-ins over a customer-configured egress endpoint (TLS). Ops/updates can be run via manifests or an optional outbound-control-plane channel. No inbound peering required unless the customer requests managed peering for Dedicated.
mike: Audit logging: will logs include prompts or only metadata? what about PII redaction?
dana: By default we log metadata: request_id, model_id, token_count, latency, route, and billing attribution. Prompt text is not logged unless customer opts in via audit-log policy. For PII handling we provide automated redaction hooks and allow customers to supply regex/redaction rules. Logs exported to S3/GCS can be encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys.
mike: Can we see an example retention policy CLI?
dana: CLI example to set 180-day retention + S3 export:
```
redwoodctl audit-config set --org org_88 --retention 180 --export s3://acme-redwood/logs --kms arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222:key/ef01
```

leo: KMS: can customer supply BYOK and require HSM? Any constraints for key policies?
dana: Yes BYOK across AWS/GCP/Azure. HSM-backed keys supported via customer KMS providers. Key policy must allow the Redwood service principal to Encrypt/Decrypt for envelope ops. Rotation and access logs remain with the customer. We're adding an HSM attestation workflow next year.

priya: Rollouts and compliance: can we lock a route to prevent auto-rollbacks to unapproved models?
dana: Yes: Console policy option "enforce_model_pin" will block fallbacks and return 403 if request would hit an unapproved model. We also ship audit hooks that record any attempted rollouts or canary activations.

dana: Next steps: 1) Publish SOC2 timeline + checklist (owner: sam) 2) Publish Private deploy security checklist (owner: ana) 3) Share CLI + manifest examples in docs (owner: leo). I'll file follow-ups in #docs after this.
sam: Ping me if you want to join the audit readiness WG. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
